title: U.S. House · Texas's 22nd District
area: Fort Bend, Brazoria and southern Harris counties, southwest of Houston.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Troy Nehls did not appear on the ballot in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for the redrawn 22nd District. His brother, Trever Nehls, won the Republican nomination with 75.7% of the vote over Rebecca Clark. Marquette Greene-Scott won the Democratic nomination outright over four other candidates.

candidates.name: Trever Nehls
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 75.7% of the vote over Rebecca Clark.

summary.text: Trever Nehls is the Republican nominee for this open southwest-Houston-area seat, previously held by his brother Troy Nehls. He holds graduate degrees in public administration and military strategic studies and founded a consulting firm.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and corrections from the University of Wisconsin–Platteville, a master's degree in public administration from Central Michigan University, and a master's degree in military strategic studies from the U.S. Army War College.
Worked in the private sector and founded Nehls Consulting, LLC.

positions.summary: His campaign website calls for ending catch-and-release permanently, finishing the border wall and deporting "illegal aliens who violate our laws".
positions.quote: Congress must help President Trump fully secure the southern border, finish the wall, end catch-and-release permanently, and deport illegal aliens who violate our laws.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content or Candidate Connection survey was located beyond Ballotpedia's biographical entry.

candidates.name: Marquette Greene-Scott
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.6% of the vote over four other candidates.

summary.text: Marquette Greene-Scott is the Democratic nominee for this open seat. She is an attorney and former math teacher who currently serves as mayor pro tem of Iowa Colony, Texas.

background.text: Born in Opelousas, Louisiana; earned a B.S. in secondary education/mathematics (1993) and an M.S. in mathematics (1997) from Southern University, and a J.D. in 2004 from the Paul M. Hebert Law Center at Louisiana State University.
Worked as a high school and college math teacher and is a practicing attorney in Texas and Louisiana.
Serves as mayor pro tem of the City of Iowa Colony, holding Position 3 on the city council.

positions.summary: In her 2026 Candidate Connection survey she calls healthcare a human right and supports universal healthcare.
positions.quote: Universal healthcare ensures that every person can get the care they need to live a healthy life.

positions.summary: In her 2026 Candidate Connection survey she says Congress must raise the minimum wage, indexing it to inflation as a first step.
positions.quote: Congress must raise minimum wage, indexing it to inflation as a first step.

positions.summary: In her 2024 Candidate Connection survey she said her top priority is reinstating reproductive rights, including access to safe abortions.
positions.quote: We must ensure access to reproductive healthcare services which include contraception, prenatal care, and safe abortions.

record.text: Serves as mayor pro tem and Position 3 city council member for the City of Iowa Colony, Texas.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey biographical section, but it did not include specific federal policy positions.
